title: Getting_started
text: workflow fairly simple. Using framrsquared package connect FRAM databases. use compare_table_across_dbs() compare values table interest two databases. suggest Mortality table, mortality values , ERs . effect, function lines values run (ie, mortality values stock 1 fishery 1 timestep 1 age 3) compares . ideal world, see exact match values run established FRAM software new FRAM software (assuming, applied runs expect case). However, may situations expect results approximately exactly (e.g., mortalities unrelated stock attempt stock splitting – exactly , may see “decimal dust”). summarize_exact() summarize_ratio() make tables absolute differences proportional differences values, plot_comparisons_exact() plot_comparisons_ratio() create diagnostic plots . case databases Formal testing/coho_preseason_notamm_c.mdb Formal testing/coho_preseason_notamm_c.mdb, basic comparison might look like following. reminder, connect_fram_db give error filepath isn’t absolute; package provides absolute filepaths based current project. cases fisheries, stocks, runs expected identical two databases, can filtered outputs compare_table_across_dbs() running summarize_*() plot_comparisons_*().
code: library(framrsquared) library(tidyverse) library(framqaqc) library(here)  fram_a = connect_fram_db(here("Formal testing/coho_preseason_notamm_a.mdb"),                          read_only = TRUE,                          quiet = TRUE) fram_c = connect_fram_db(here("Formal testing/coho_preseason_notamm_c.mdb"),                          read_only = TRUE,                          quiet = TRUE)                           mortality_comparison = compare_table_across_dbs(fram_a, fram_c, "Mortality")  summarize_exact(mortality_comparison) #hopefully all 0s or close to 0 summarize_ratio(mortality_comparison) #hopefully all 1s or close to 1  plot_comparisons_exact(mortality_comparison) #hopefully all points are on or near the 1:1 line plot_comparisons_ratio(mortality_comparison) #hopefully all points are on or the y = 1 line  disconnect_fram_db(fram_a) disconnect_fram_db(fram_c)

title: Compare tables in two equivalent FRAM databases — compare_databases
text: key output $ratios tibble, contains every comparison relevant table entries long-form. comparisons implemented first aligning corresponding table rows using appropriate key columns (e.g. run_id, fishery_id, stock_id, age, time_step, etc). $ratios, table variable columns specify table column compared, respectively. prop_err, abs_err, scale_err provide measures changes "original" value (fram_db_1) "comparison" value (fram_db_2). . original new columns give actual values compared. run_id time_step specify rows compared. bkfram_off_by_fish bkfram_off_by_prop provide context comparison (). Quantifying error FRAM involves numerical solvers, expect small differences table entries even comparing two effectively equivalent databases. compare_databases() provides three metrics changes. case, assumed fram_db_1 reference file; "error" measures show much  value fram_db_2 changed relative corresponding value fram_db_1. simplest measure error abs_err. absolute value difference two values. looking entry table = "Mortality" variable = "landed_catch", abs.err 5 means fram_db_2 entry five fish less fram_db_1 entry. can confirm looking original new columns. abs_err easily interpreted, often meaningful looking across tables variables. , abs_err value 5 mean relatively meaningless change five fish landed catch entry originally thousands fish, value 5 huge change fishing effort fishery scaler entry. One way make error comparable across tables variables calculate proportional error. entry changed 0.01%, meaningful, changed 10%, . $prop_err provides proportional error, -0.5 means entry fram_db_2 50% less corresponding value fram_db_1, value 2 means entry fram_db_2 200% corresponding value fram_db_1. ' gives error context original value, often good way look problems. However, sometimes find large $prop_err values changes concerning. example, may entry landed catch mortality table 0.00001 fish fram_db_1, 0 fish fram_db_2. practicality two values identical, 0.00001 fish difference likely one random jitter numerical solver rounding differences. However, $prop_err value cell -1, extreme negative change can get. can jointly look $abs_err $prop_err address potential misleadingly large errors $prop_err, nice single error metric provides error context without sensitive small entries fram_db_1. scale_err elaboration $prop_err provides broader context. $prop_err takes absolute error scales original value fram_db_1. $scale_err generalizes idea, first calculating average error table-variable combination, scaling absolute error corresponding table-variable average. , entry landed_catch Mortality table 0.001 fram_db_1, 0.002 fram_db_2, average landed_catch entries fram_db_1 1000, prop_err 1 (since fram_db_2 double value fram_db_1, (0.002-0.001)/0.001), scale.err 0.000001 ((0.002-0.001)/1000). better captures intuition difference 0.001 fish landed catch big deal, since values typically huge. scale_err thus measure error comparable across variables tables, essentially answer question "entry changed lot kind variable table?". scale_err frequently useful error metric, compare_databases() provides three. may contexts important focus proportional error. example, large proportional errors landed catch catch rare stocks can important, much larger catch stock water scale_err metric. Addressing backwardsFRAM wiggle post-season runs, backwards FRAM algorithm employed; solver stops estimated fish numbers within 1 fish target size. means potential substantial "wiggle" bkFRAm values comparing two databases. wiggle can propagate tables, especially stock-age-timesteps target values quite small (wiggle +/- 1 fish proportionally large amount). reason, can useful see measures error correspond errors corresponding bk fram table. every table entry makes sense (e.g., stock id, age, timestep), $bkfram_off_by_fish gives absolute error corresponding row BackwardsFram table, bkfram_off_by_prop give relative error (proportion) corresponding row BackwardsFram table. bkfram wiggle cause observed errors, expect largest errors correspond largest $bkfram_off_by_fish $bkfram_off_by_prop values. Suggestions simple plotting see original new values fall 1:1 line, ggplot2::geom_point() can used, $ratios$original $ratios$new x y, facet_wrap table (perhaps variable) make plots readable. identifying meaningful change, scale.err likely best measure error. can helpful plot scale.err bkfram...fish bkfram...prop see table entries largest error correspond stock-fishery-age-timestep largest wiggle backwards fram solutions. digging individual tables, can sometimes helpful look comparisons $ratios_detailed, contains additional columns fit standardized formatting $ratios.
